content.text: I have what I need. The grant, definitions, and assignment clause together determine the outcome.

input.quote: 23.4 Customer's Right to Obtain the Source Code. M&I hereby grants to Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable license, through the end of the Term, to use the source code (including the right to make modifications thereto) on the terms and conditions set forth in this Article 23, upon payment of the then current license fees and the occurrence of the following events:
input.rationale: The operative licence grant is the Article 23 source-code licence (p0310). It satisfies the rule's material terms: (i) affiliate coverage is automatic and needs no notice, because "Customer" is defined in the preamble as "Tri City National Bank ... (including its Affiliates, 'Customer')" (p0016), reinforced by §21.10 (all processing for Customer's subsidiaries and Affiliates is covered) and §21.11.A (newly acquired financial institutions fall automatically within "Customer") — this exceeds the fallback, which only requires affiliates on written notice; (ii) contractors acting on our behalf are accommodated, since §23.5 expressly permits use by "Customer (or its designee)" for our internal processing needs; and (iii) the licence is not revocable at M&I's discretion — it is triggered by M&I's own failure (cessation of business, refusal to provide Services, or bankruptcy) and contains no vendor revocation right, so it is well clear of the walk-away position. On transferability, although the grant is labelled "non-transferable", §22.4 allows us to assign the Agreement (and with it Article 23) without M&I's consent in a qualifying merger, meeting the fallback's successor-transfer requirement. Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred drafting and are noted rather than redlined: the licence runs only "through the end of the Term" rather than being perpetual/irrevocable notwithstanding payment of the then-current licence fees, and the internal-use and no-sublicence restrictions in §23.5 are drawn tightly around the designee concept. Neither defeats the fallback, so we would not open this clause; if Article 23 is reopened for other reasons we would seek perpetual survival of the licence once the fees are paid.
